There are two shrines of the same name, one in former {{ill|Shirahama, Wakayama|ar|شيراهاما واكاياما|arz|شيراهاما واكاياما|ceb|Shirahama-chō|de|Shirahama (Wakayama)|es|Shirahama (Wakayama)|fa|شیراهاما، واکایاما|fr|Shirahama|it|Shirahama|ja|白浜町|ko|시라하마정|ms|Shirahama, Wakayama|my|ရှိရဟမမြို့၊ ဝါခါယာမ|nl|Shirahama (Wakayama)|pl|Shirahama|ru|Сирахама|simple|Shirahama, Wakayama|sv|Shirahama|tl|Shirahama, Wakayama|tr|Shirahama|uk|Сірахама|ur|شیراہاما، واکایاما|vi|Shirahama, Wakayama|zh|白濱町|qid=Q1202728}} and one in former {{ill|Chikura, Chiba|fa|چیکورا، چیبا|ja|千倉町|ko|지쿠라정|ur|چیکورا، چیبا|qid=Q5097510}}. Both enshrine {{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|ko|아메노히와시노카미|zh|天日鷲神|qid=Q10939697|lt=Ame-no-Hiwashi-no-Mikoto}} as principal deity and claim succession to the {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} "Shimotate Matsubara Shrine" of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ceb|Awa (baranggay)|ckb|پارێزگای ئاوا (چیبا)|cs|Provincie Awa (Čiba)|de|Provinz Awa (Chiba)|es|Provincia de Awa (Chiba)|fa|ولایت آوا (چیبا)|fr|Province d'Awa (Chiba)|gl|Provincia de Awa, Chiba|hak|Awa-koet (Tōkaidō)|id|Provinsi Awa (Chiba)|it|Awa (provincia, Chiba)|ja|安房国|ko|아와국 (도카이도)|lt|Avos žemė (Čiba)|nl|Awa (provincie in Chiba)|pt|Província de Awa (Chiba)|ru|Ава (Канто)|simple|Awa Province (Chiba)|sk|Awa (provincia, Čiba)|sr|Провинција Ава (Хоншу)|tr|Awa (vilayet, Chiba)|uk|Провінція Ава (Канто)|zh|安房國|zh_min_nan|Awa-kok (Tôkaidô)|zh_yue|安房國|qid=Q1053044}}{{ill|Asai District, Chiba|ja|朝夷郡|simple|Asai District, Chiba|qid=Q4803406}}. This was long disputed, but no decisive evidence emerged and both claims remain.

Both shrine traditions say it began when Yubutsu-nushi-no-Mikoto, grandson of Ame-no-Hiwashi-no-Mikoto who came to Awa with {{ill|Amatomi no Mikoto|ja|天富命|qid=Q24899653}}, enshrined Ame-no-Hiwashi-no-Mikoto in the first year of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ar|الإمبراطور جينمو|arz|الامبراطور جينمو|as|জিম্মু|az|Cimmu|bcl|Emperador Jimmu|be|Імператар Дзіму|ca|Jinmu|cdo|Sìng-ū Tiĕng-huòng|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر جینمو|cs|Džimmu|de|Jimmu|el|Αυτοκράτορας Τζίμου|eo|Imperiestro Jinmu|es|Jinmu Tennō|et|Jimmu|eu|Jimmu enperadorea|fa|امپراتور جینمو|fi|Jinmu|fr|Jinmu|hak|Sṳ̀n-vú Thiên-fòng|he|ג'ימו, קיסר יפן|hi|सम्राट जिममु|hr|Jinmu|hu|Dzsinmu japán császár|id|Jimmu|it|Jinmu|ja|神武天皇|jv|Jimmu Tenno|ka|ძიმუ|ko|진무 천황|kw|Emperour Jimmu|la|Jimmu|lt|Imperatorius Džinmu|lv|Džimmu|mn|Эзэн Хаан Жиммү|mr|जिम्मू|ms|Maharaja Jimmu|my|ဂျင်းမူ ဧကရာဇ်|nl|Jimmu|no|Jimmu|pl|Jimmu|pt|Jimmu|ru|Император Дзимму|sh|Car Jimmu|simple|Emperor Jimmu|sl|Cesar Džinmu|sr|Џинму|sv|Jimmu|th|จักรพรรดิจิมมุ|tl|Emperador Jimmu|tr|Jimmu|uk|Імператор Дзімму|uz|Jimmu|vi|Thiên hoàng Jimmu|war|Emperador Jimmu|wuu|神武天皇|zh|神武天皇|zh_classical|神武天皇|zh_min_nan|Sîn-bú Thian-hông|zh_yue|神武天皇|qid=Q200188}}.

''Gikeiki'' records that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ar|ميناموتو نو يوريتومو|be|Мінамота-но Ёрытома|bg|Минамото но Йоритомо|br|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ca|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ckb|مینامۆتۆ نۆ یۆریتۆمۆ|cs|Joritomo Minamoto|de|Minamoto no Yoritomo|el|Μιναμότο νο Γιοριτόμο|eo|Minamoto no Yoritomo|es|Minamoto no Yoritomo|eu|Minamoto no Yoritomo|fa|میناموتو نو یوریتومو|fi|Minamoto no Yoritomo|fr|Minamoto no Yoritomo|hak|Minamoto no Yoritomo|he|מינאמוטו נו יוריטומו|hu|Minamoto no Joritomo|id|Minamoto no Yoritomo|it|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝|ko|미나모토노 요리토모|la|Minamoto no Yoritomo|lt|Minamoto no Joritomo|mr|मिनामोटो नो योरिमोटो|ms|Minamoto no Yoritomo|nl|Minamoto no Yoritomo|pl|Yoritomo Minamoto|pt|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ro|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ru|Минамото-но Ёритомо|sh|Minamoto no Yoritomo|sk|Joritomo Minamoto|sl|Minamoto no Joritomo|sq|Minamoto no Joritomo|sr|Минамото но Јоритомо|sv|Minamoto no Yoritomo|th|มินาโมโตะ โนะ โยริโตโมะ|tl|Minamoto no Yoritomo|tr|Minamoto no Yoritomo|uk|Мінамото-но Йорітомо|vi|Minamoto no Yoritomo|war|Minamoto no Yoritomo|wuu|源赖朝|zh|源赖朝|zh_min_nan|Minamoto no Yoritomo|zh_yue|源賴朝|zu|Minamoto no Yoritomo|qid=Q242800}}, after defeat at {{ill|Battle of Ishibashiyama|ar|معركة إيشيباشي-ياما|ca|Batalla d'Ishibashiyama|de|Schlacht von Ishibashiyama|es|Batalla de Ishibashiyama|fa|نبرد ایشی‌باشی‌یاما|fr|Bataille d'Ishibashiyama|it|Battaglia di Ishibashiyama|ja|石橋山の戦い|pl|Bitwa pod Ishibashiyamą|pt|Batalha de Ishibashiyama|sv|Slaget vid Ishibashiyama|vi|Trận Ishibashiyama|zh|石橋山之戰|qid=Q2888010}}, fled to Awa; after worship at {{ill|Susaki Shrine|ja|洲崎神社|simple|Susaki Shrine|qid=Q11556513}}, he spent one night at Takiguchi Daimyōjin (this shrine). Before the Edo period it was called "Kotaka Myōjin" and "Takiguchi Myōjin."

A tradition says many deer lived in the area and troubled residents when Ame-no-Tomi-no-Mikoto and others landed in Awa, so deer hunting was performed. Based on this, a ritual hunt festival was held for ten days from old calendar November 26.

To the right of the haiden is Ten Shrine enshrining Amenominakanushi-no-Mikoto. It is a Shikinaisha that was merged into this shrine in 1928. The former Ten Shrine building was moved into these precincts and used as a mikoshi hall; later, after a new mikoshi hall was built, it was restored as the Ten Shrine building.

It is said that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ar|ميناموتو نو يوريتومو|be|Мінамота-но Ёрытома|bg|Минамото но Йоритомо|br|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ca|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ckb|مینامۆتۆ نۆ یۆریتۆمۆ|cs|Joritomo Minamoto|de|Minamoto no Yoritomo|el|Μιναμότο νο Γιοριτόμο|eo|Minamoto no Yoritomo|es|Minamoto no Yoritomo|eu|Minamoto no Yoritomo|fa|میناموتو نو یوریتومو|fi|Minamoto no Yoritomo|fr|Minamoto no Yoritomo|hak|Minamoto no Yoritomo|he|מינאמוטו נו יוריטומו|hu|Minamoto no Joritomo|id|Minamoto no Yoritomo|it|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝|ko|미나모토노 요리토모|la|Minamoto no Yoritomo|lt|Minamoto no Joritomo|mr|मिनामोटो नो योरिमोटो|ms|Minamoto no Yoritomo|nl|Minamoto no Yoritomo|pl|Yoritomo Minamoto|pt|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ro|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ru|Минамото-но Ёритомо|sh|Minamoto no Yoritomo|sk|Joritomo Minamoto|sl|Minamoto no Joritomo|sq|Minamoto no Joritomo|sr|Минамото но Јоритомо|sv|Minamoto no Yoritomo|th|มินาโมโตะ โนะ โยริโตโมะ|tl|Minamoto no Yoritomo|tr|Minamoto no Yoritomo|uk|Мінамото-но Йорітомо|vi|Minamoto no Yoritomo|war|Minamoto no Yoritomo|wuu|源赖朝|zh|源赖朝|zh_min_nan|Minamoto no Yoritomo|zh_yue|源賴朝|zu|Minamoto no Yoritomo|qid=Q242800}}, who later opened the Kamakura shogunate, dedicated statues of Yoriyoshi and Yoshie and an image of Yakushi Nyorai to the branch Mitama Shirahata Shrine here, along with 600 volumes of the Great Prajñā Sutra copied by himself.
